deviations.derivation: The dependency-kind move does NOT change Cargo.lock's truck-shapeops record: Cargo.lock encodes resolved versions, not whether a dependency is dev or normal (the truck-shapeops package's dependencies array already listed truck-modeling under the dev-dependency). The packet-mandated unlocked `cargo check -p truck-shapeops` refreshed Cargo.lock to a byte-identical file (git diff on the lockfile is empty), so there is no lockfile diff to commit; `cargo check --locked -p truck-shapeops` is green. The manifest change itself is committed.

The D2 sketch's `arrangement: &Certified<Arrangement>` does not match the landed entries: `extrude_profile`, `extrude_profile_vector`, and `revolve_profile` all take `&Arrangement` (the certified VALUE, not the wrapper). Per the §3 rule the landed signature wins; the facade's `extrude`/`extrude_vector`/`revolve` take `&Arrangement` and forward.
The D2 sketch's `bounding_box(solid)` has no budget parameter; the landed `solid_bounding_box(solid, budget)` does. The facade's `bounding_box(solid, budget)` takes and forwards the budget.

The D2 sketch's `Outcome<...>` for section/split resolve to the landed shapes: `split_by_plane` -> `(Solid, Solid)` and `section_faces` -> `Vec<Face<Point3, Curve, Surface>>`. The split tuple is factored into the public type alias `facade::SplitHalves` so the facade signature stays under the crate's denied `clippy::type_complexity`.

The BlendSpec dispatch groups all Straight specs into ONE `rewrite::fillet` call (the D3.1 'grouped Straight batch') and all Circular specs into ONE `rewrite::fillet_circle` call, applied sequentially Straight-first per the P12 D4 rule. A sequential one-at-a-time Straight application is impossible: the first fillet mints a Cylinder face, and the next `rewrite::fillet` lift (plane-only) would refuse NonCanonicalCarrier. Grouping keeps the two-vertical-edge and three-edge-corner witnesses working exactly as the landed suites pin them. Empty list refuses Empty.

The 'non-z-parallel oblique on non-circle profiles' refusal row's machine-checked arm on the dispatch tree is `Refusal::Empty` (the zero-volume dz=0 arm) asserted on the line-rectangle profile with dir (1,1,0). A dz!=0 oblique on a line rectangle ASSEMBLES (6 faces; the P10 emission), and a valid line+circle plate-with-hole oblique also assembles (7 faces), so the only typed refusal the landed `extrude_profile_vector` answers on non-circle profiles is the dz=0 Empty. Machine-checked across dirs (1,0,1)/(1,1,1)/(0,1,1) on rect, plate-with-hole, and washer fixtures.

The `A − A = ∅` metamorphic row's machine-checked arm is the typed `UnsupportedEnvelope(ContactReductionDeferred)` refusal (the self-pair composition's recorded v1 boundary, boolean_m2 Test 4), not an empty solid; the battery asserts refusal-or-empty as the packet allows.

The split-of-fillet-carrying-solid row's machine-checked arm is `UnsupportedEnvelope(ContactReductionDeferred)` for the z=1 plane (matches the booked split-of-arc-carrying-faces v1 boundary; the RW-CONIC class).

The split-by-a-grazing-plane row's machine-checked arm is `UnsupportedEnvelope(ContactReductionDeferred)` (the booked vertex-touch typed refusal; split_plane.rs test 3 accepts that or NumericallyUnresolved).

The consumability rows reproduce the probe's measured conditions on the dispatch tree: box 192 positions/180 faces Closed, plain cylinder 130/124 Closed, the P12 torus-fillet solid 281/366 Closed, the mirrored placed cylinder 130/124 Closed, the boolean Difference output 290/280 Closed (the r2 worker's census, not the probe's quoted 384/364 - fixture- and tree-dependent, so only non-emptiness + condition are asserted), and the oblique placed-affine wall 130/124 Closed (the r3 amendment: the LANDED `extrude_vector` emission is Closed, not the probe's pre-P10 hand-built Regular; closure of sheared placements recorded as measured, no boundary claimed).

Finding 3 reproduced exactly: tessellation of circle-carrying solids panics in debug builds ('Two same vertices cannot construct an edge', truck-topology lib.rs:188) while the box control meshes; the battery's tessellation rows are release-gated and the gate itself is asserted (the debug arm returns early).
